svg.title: A standard atomless compact-extraction counterexample under CH
svg.desc: Under the continuum hypothesis, a locally compact refinement of Cantor topology has countable compact neighborhoods, hereditarily separable finite powers, and exactly the ordinary Cantor Borel sigma-algebras in every finite power. One-point compactification and a torus orbit mixture produce the entire seed list of Theorem 3.23, including the actual product-Borel condition. The independent shift and an irrational circle rotation give the final invariant ergodic fully supported standard atomless probability and pointwise free compact action. Compact subsets of its conull carrier project to null compact seed subsets. No existence claim without CH is made.
svg.text: The complete standard atomless counterexample · under CH
Theorem 3.29 · CH means 2ℵ₀ = ℵ₁ · no existence assertion without CH
Actual Cantor points; a finer locally compact topology · 3.24–3.25
C = 2N, enumerated as {cξ : ξ < ω₁}; ρ ordinary Cantor topology; τ ⊃ ρ
Every countable finite-power set Sμ is coded before later closure requirements.
At ξ: disjoint compact-clopen Kk approach cξ in ρ.
Nm = {cξ} ∪ ⋃k≥m Kk is a countable compact-open neighborhood.
Finite-power Borel equality proved · Lemma 3.26 / Theorem 3.27
Every τn-closed F has countable dense S; let Mj(S) use ρ in coordinate j.
Off repeated-coordinate diagonals D and a countable Q:
F = ⋂j Mj(S); each mixed closure is ordinary product-Borel.
B(Cn, τn) = B(Cn, ρn) for all finite n. No ordinal-order Borel partition is used.
Compactification of the line · Proposition 3.28
Y = (C, τ); every compact subset of Y is countable, hence η-null.
η = fair-coin Cantor probability on the exact actual Borel sigma-algebra.
D = Y ∪ {∞} compact Hausdorff; clopen coordinates embed D into TI, |I| ≤ continuum.
Full support and the entire seed · Propositions 3.20 / 3.28
K = T{*} ⊔ I; j(D) has distinguished coordinate 0; translated levels Dk are disjoint.
ν = Σk∈ℤ (2−|k|/3) (translationk ∘ j)* η; V = ⋃k Yk conull and actually standard.
Compact subsets of V are null. Each finite power has countably many closed level strata.
Their Borel equalities give B(Vr) = B(V)⊗r. The intermediate torus action is nonergodic.
The final action and measure · Theorems 3.23 / 3.29
X = Kℤ × T; E = Vℤ × T; μ = ι*((ν|V)ℤ ⊗ ℓ)
T(x, z) = (σx, z + α); α irrational; (σx)j = xj+1
Independent shift mixing + circle Fourier coefficients ⇒ ergodicity.
nα ∈ ℤ ⇒ n = 0: free at every ambient point. Full support, invariant probability.
E actual Borel, conull and standard; μ atomless; X separable compact Hausdorff.
The actual compact-extraction failure
L ⊂ E compact ⇒ π0(L) ⊂ V compact ⇒ μ(L) ≤ ν(π0(L)) = 0.
Yet μ(E) = 1. Exercise 5.24 gives a Borel event B ⊂ E with μ(B) = 1/36.
No positive compact subset exists; the regular and atomic positive branches remain intact.
Proof locators: (3.51)–(3.56) recursion; (3.59)–(3.61) Borel proof; (3.62)–(3.65) full seed and action.

a.text: Topological method: de la Vega and Kunen, A Compact Homogeneous S-space, §2, Theorem 2.4.
Source being tested: Takesaki III, XIII.1, Exercise 5(a), pp. 11–12.
